hero.title: Questions we get asked about GEO
hero.answer: HARGILE makes businesses visible in AI answers and on Google. Here are the direct answers to the questions people ask before getting started: how long, what results, how it works, and how much it costs.

items.q: What exactly is GEO?
items.a: GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization. It is the work that gets your business named when someone asks an AI assistant a question: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Overviews. These assistants cite sources. GEO makes your site one of those sources: machine-readable content, structured data, clear answers to the questions your buyers actually ask.

items.q: How do I know if AI already mentions me?
items.a: We run the 25 questions your buyers actually ask AI, and we look at who gets cited: you, your competitors, or nobody. That is the free audit, and it is the first step. You get the results, with no commitment.

items.q: Does GEO replace SEO?
items.a: No. GEO builds on SEO. The foundation is the same: a fast, well-structured, readable site serves SEO and GEO alike. What GEO adds is the lens of answer engines: making your content not just indexable by Google, but citable by AI. We do both, because they reinforce each other.

items.q: What types of businesses benefit most from GEO?
items.a: Service businesses whose clients research before choosing: accountants and fiduciaries, law firms, notaries, consultants, recruiters, architects. Not on the list? If a prospect might ask an AI "who does X in Y" and you do X in Y, GEO is for you.

items.q: How long until we see results?
items.a: Technical fixes (speed, structure, structured data) show effects within weeks. Content work takes longer: expect three to six months for significant movement on Google. On the AI-citation side, the first changes often come faster, because models refresh their sources regularly. We track the numbers with you from day one.

items.q: Do you guarantee first position on Google?
items.a: No, and nobody honest can: Google's algorithm is not ours to control, and neither are the AI models. What we commit to is the method, and full transparency about what it produces. An agency that guarantees you first place has already told you something about the rest.

items.q: How do GEO and SEO work together?
items.a: SEO makes your site findable on Google. GEO makes your business citable by AI assistants. The work overlaps heavily: structured data, fast site, clear content written around your clients' real questions. We treat it as one workflow, because the same optimizations feed both channels. A page that ranks well on Google is already halfway to being cited by AI; the other half is what we add.

items.q: How does the free audit work?
items.a: You give us your website URL. We identify the 25 questions your buyers ask AI in your industry, run them through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude, and record who gets cited. We also check your Google position on those same queries. You get a written report, with no commitment and no payment. If there is room to improve, we explain what we would do. If there isn't, we tell you that too.

items.q: What's included in the monthly service?
items.a: Three things. First, AI-citation monitoring: we track whether answer engines mention you, and for which questions. Second, optimization, content and technical: schema.org structured data, on-page improvements, writing or rewriting pages when needed. Third, reporting: Google rankings, organic traffic, AI citations, in a shared dashboard. What is not included: paid advertising, social media management, link-buying. We do the work that makes your site citable, not the work that games the algorithm. No 40-page report: the numbers that matter, whenever you want them.

items.q: How do we track results?
items.a: With shared numbers. Google rankings, organic traffic and AI citations are in a dashboard you have access to: the same numbers we look at, at the same time. No cherry-picked metrics, no report that only shows the good news. If something isn't working, you see it when we do.

hero.title: Your visibility, automated

geo.title: How do you get cited by AI?
geo.lead: When a client asks ChatGPT or Perplexity which agency builds web applications in Brussels, the assistant answers by citing its sources. Being one of those sources is where visibility now starts, and it is worked page by page.
summary: Be cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini, not just found on Google.
First technical effects within weeks, content effects within months.
Presence measured on 25 real questions from your industry, in French and Dutch.

readable.title: Content machines can read
readable.text: The answers are in the HTML on the first load, with no JavaScript to run. An engine that only sees an empty page cites nothing.

structured.title: Structured data
structured.text: Every page states what it is and who wrote it, in schema.org format. That is what lets the engine attach an answer to one specific company.

answers.title: One page, one real question
answers.text: Every page answers, plainly, a question your clients actually ask. That is the format answer engines quote and attribute.

geo.conditions: Three conditions, in the order an answer engine meets them:

demo.question: Who do you recommend for [your trade] in [your city]?

before.label: Today
before.caption: Your company is missing. The AI has nothing to cite.

after.label: After the work
after.caption: Your site answers the question: the AI cites you.

process.title: How we work
process.lead: Each step says what the system does and what we do ourselves.

audit.title: Audit
audit.text: The facts on day one: what makes you visible, what holds you back, and where the queries that matter to your business are. We also measure your starting point in AI answers, before touching anything.
audit.system: mobile speed, Chrome field data, robots, sitemap, full site crawl.
audit.us: choosing the queries, the AI questions and the competitors to track.

tech.title: Technical
tech.text: A site engines can read without obstacles: speed, structure, structured data, content present from the first load.
tech.system: page titles and descriptions, proposed then applied to your CMS after approval.
tech.us: schema.org, hreflang, canonical, performance, done by hand and checked.

content.title: Content
content.text: Pages that each answer one real customer question, the format Google and answer engines cite.
content.us: the writing, with you, in your own vocabulary: revisions, new pages, blog articles when they are needed.
content.system: flags, from the questions we track, the texts to revise, the pages that are missing and the article topics to write.

measure.title: Measure
measure.text: We start from the starting point measured on day one (the baseline) and track what changes.
measure.system: your presence and your competitors' in the answers of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and Google AI Overviews, on 25 real customer questions, in French and Dutch; rankings and traffic reviewed with you at every check-in.
measure.us: choosing the competitors to compare, reading, deciding, adjusting, at every check-in with you.

approval.title: Nothing is written to your site without your consent
approval.text: The system does not edit your site live. It proposes. Every recommendation becomes a proposal: the page concerned, the current value, the proposed value, and why.

validate.title: Approval mode
validate.text: You receive every proposal and accept or reject it. Nothing goes out without your click. This is the default.

auto.title: Automatic mode
auto.text: You trust us with routine changes (titles, descriptions): proposals we have approved are applied every morning, under a daily cap you set. You can switch back to approval mode at any time.

rules: The system never replaces a value it has not read first.
Every write is checked afterwards and logged: what, when, before, after.
On the first failed write, the pilot stops by itself and alerts us.
Your changes live in your CMS, not with us. If you leave, they stay.

card.title: Proposal
card.after: Web development, GEO and SEO for SMEs in Brussels. Free audit within 48 h.
card.why: Why: description too short (12 characters), the page names neither the trade nor the city.

access.title: Your credentials
access.text: Your credentials are never stored in our database. They live in an encrypted vault, and every read is traced: who, when, what for. To stop, one message is enough: we remove the subscription from our CRM, the system reads nothing more, nothing breaks.

revoke.title: Stop on request
revoke.text: One message, and we remove the subscription.

access.platforms: WordPress (Yoast, Rank Math, The SEO Framework) and Shopify: approved proposals are applied automatically. Webflow and custom-built sites: same audit, same proposals, applied by us, by hand or in the code.

metaProof.title: Architecture & source
metaProof.text: The method we propose is the one we apply to our own site. View this page's source: it is all there.
points: Every page exists in French and English, with the tags that tell engines which one to serve.
Every page carries its structured data (schema.org), validated automatically before every release.
All the content is in the HTML from the first response, readable by search engines and AI assistants alike.

measured.title: This page, in numbers
measured.lead: Measured on {date} on this very page, with {tool}, under mobile conditions. You can run the tool yourself and land on the same figures, and that is the whole point of publishing them.
measured.note: The main content paint is still over its 2.5 second threshold, and we leave it on display rather than picking the numbers that suit us. That one is work in progress. An agency that only publishes its good scores is not telling you what it measures: it is telling you what it shows.

measures.title: What we measure and what we don't promise
measures.text: You don't have to take our word for it. We look at the same numbers you do, at the same time, against a baseline taken on day one.
points: Your presence in AI answers, and that of the competitors you choose: mentions, share of voice (the proportion of answers that cite your brand), average position, and whether your domain is used as a source. On 25 real customer questions, in FR and NL, across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and Google AI Overviews.
Rankings on the queries that matter to your business, not the ones that look good in a report, reviewed with you at every check-in.
Organic traffic, with the honest timeline: a few weeks for technical work, several months for content.
measures.refusal: What we will not sell: a guaranteed first position, or the certainty of being cited by AI. Nobody controls Google's algorithm, nobody controls the models, and no tool "pushes" a site into their answers. An agency that promises you otherwise controls the algorithm and the models no more than we do. What we commit to: the method, and transparency about what it produces.
measures.cadence: Cadence: a full analysis every two weeks (weekly or monthly on request), approved proposals applied every morning, a shared check-in with you at every analysis.

proofCase.text: VENIZI sells its jewellery online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France: a catalogue where every product has to be findable.

items.q: How long before we see results?
items.a: SEO is a long-term investment: technical fixes show effects within weeks, content within months. It is slower than advertising, but it does not stop when the budget does.

items.q: Do you guarantee the first position on Google?
items.a: No, and nobody serious can: results depend on an algorithm nobody controls. What we do guarantee is the method: clean technical foundations, content that answers real questions, measurement, and transparency about what it produces.

items.q: What does being visible in AI answers mean?
items.a: When someone asks ChatGPT or Perplexity which agency can build a web application in Brussels, those assistants cite their sources. Being cited is the new ranking, and it can be worked on: machine-readable content, structured data, and clear answers to the questions people actually ask.

items.q: How do we track results?
items.a: You do not have to take our word for it: rankings, organic traffic and cited pages are tracked and shared. We look at the same numbers you do.

items.q: What do you change on my site, and who decides?
items.a: Nothing is written without approval. Every recommendation is filed with the current value and the proposed value. You accept or reject it, or you hand us routine changes in automatic mode, under a daily cap. Everything is checked after writing and logged.

items.q: Which CMS?
items.a: WordPress (Yoast, Rank Math, The SEO Framework) and Shopify for automatic application. Webflow and custom-built sites: we do the audit and the proposals, and we apply them ourselves, by hand or in the code.

items.q: What do you do with my credentials?
items.a: They are never stored in our database. They live in an encrypted vault, every read is traced. To stop, one message is enough: we remove the subscription and the system reads nothing more.

items.q: What if I stop?
items.a: One message, and we remove the subscription from our CRM. The changes live in your CMS, they stay. We delete nothing, and we hand you the baseline and the log.

items.q: Is the content written by an AI?
items.a: No. The pages are written with you. What the system automates is the analysis, the technical proposals and the measurement.

cta.text: Enter your website URL. We hand you the facts within 48 h: what holds your site back today, and your starting point in AI answers on the questions of your trade.

hero.title: Custom web applications for SMEs
hero.answer: We design, build and maintain custom web applications entirely in-house, from Brussels. No outsourcing: the team that designs your product is the one that codes it and keeps it alive. And on delivery, the code and the data belong to you.

madeInHouse.title: Everything happens in-house
madeInHouse.lead: Designed, built and maintained by the same team, in Brussels. Here is what that adds up to: every square is a site that is live today. Click one, you are there.

grid.hint: Newest first. Click a square to open the site.

ownership.title: Your code, your data
ownership.text: On delivery you own the code and your data. You can leave, host elsewhere, or keep going with us, by choice.

deliverables.title: What you receive
deliverables.lead: At the end of a project, four things are yours. Nothing stays with us: everything is designed and built in-house in Brussels, never subcontracted, and what comes out of it leaves with you.

design.text: Screens and user journeys, drawn by the same team that then codes them. You get the mockups, not only the result on screen.

code.titleRest: in a repository under your name
code.text: All of the code, in a repository you own. Another team can pick it up without having to ask us for anything.

live.text: Deployed on your own domain, in one language or several: a trilingual site is a routine request here, not an exotic add-on.

keys.text: Hosting, domain, analytics: the accounts are in your name and handed over to you. You stay with us by choice, never because the door is shut.

priceMethod.title: How the price is set
priceMethod.text: There is no honest single rate for a custom application: the price depends on what there is to build. What we commit to is the method: the price is settled during scoping, announced before development starts, and does not move afterwards.
points: The scope is frozen during scoping: the price matches that scope, in writing.
No billing by time spent, so no overrun discovered along the way.
An idea that comes up mid-project is quoted separately: you decide whether to take it or keep it for later, and the initial price does not change.
priceMethod.note: For a first product, the MVP in 30 days offer applies the same method, with a fixed price and a launch date both known from the start.

design.text: The design starts from your business, not from a template. Mockups and user flows are drawn in-house, with you.

build.text: Developed with modern web technologies, like this site. No plugin assembly: code we know line by line.

maintain.text: After launch, the foundations keep being cared for. You stay by choice, never out of necessity.

cases.title: Three proofs rather than a promise

edb.text: A generic WordPress rebuilt into a digital experience worthy of a school that deserved better.

marquisette.text: A 19th-century cottage in the heart of the Belgian Ardennes: a trilingual showcase site with integrated booking.

venizi.text: Venetian-inspired jewellery, sold online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France.

items.q: Do you take over an existing site or application?
items.a: Yes. A good share of our projects are rebuilds or takeovers: we audit what exists, keep what holds, and rebuild what blocks you. Ecole du Bonheur arrived with a generic WordPress; it left with a site worthy of its educational project.

items.q: Can you build a multilingual site?
items.a: Yes, in Belgium it is almost a habit. La Marquisette is a trilingual site with integrated booking, and this very site is served in French and English with search optimisation for each language.

items.q: Do you do the design too?
items.a: Yes. Design and development are done by the same team, in-house. You do not have to coordinate a design agency and a developer: mockups, user flows and code come from the same place.

items.q: Do you build e-commerce?
items.a: Yes. VENIZI sells its jewellery online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France. Online store, payment, catalogue: we build what your sales actually need.
